strengths: The paper addresses an important question about what multimodal contrastive learning recovers, using a potentially useful distinction between noisy coupled factors and modality-specific factors.
Synthetic experiments examine several distributional and geometric assumption violations and report strong recovery in the tested settings.
The proposed CLIP postprocessing is simple, and experiments cover four backbones, multiple few-shot settings, and four ImageNet distribution shifts, with several reported improvements.
weaknesses: The central proofs contain a fundamental error. Appendix A.4.1, Eq. (27), and A.5.1, Eq. (49), require identical embeddings for every positive pair. The assumed vMF and exponential coupling distributions have full support, so this condition forces constant embeddings, contradicting the claimed uniform, information-preserving representations. Alignment and uniformity cannot be minimized independently as asserted. Consequently, the reduction supporting both identifiability conclusions is not established.

The convex-body proof additionally assumes an unjustified uniform marginal. Eq. (56) substitutes a uniform p(z_t), whereas Lemma 4.2 establishes only convergence toward uniformity as lambda approaches zero. At finite lambda, boundary-dependent conditional normalization generally makes this marginal nonuniform, even on an interval. The stated theorem does not impose the required limit, undermining its cross-entropy reduction.

The theoretical justification for FastICA does not follow from orthogonal identifiability. The assumed uniform spherical distribution is rotationally invariant and has dependent coordinates; ICA therefore cannot select a uniquely identifiable latent orientation under this model. The proposed PCA bridge from spherical CLIP features to convex-body guarantees is also heuristic, without an approximation bound or recovery result.

The downstream experiments do not isolate the benefit of ICA or disentanglement. Appendix A.8 uses 300 ICA components or 160/200 components after PCA, without dimension-matched PCA and whitening baselines. An orthogonal ICA rotation after whitening preserves the hypothesis class and L2 penalty of the reported logistic regression. Dimensionality reduction and whitening are therefore essential alternative explanations for the gains.

CelebA evidence consists of selected decoder traversals and a subjective count of 16 attributes. Comparing this count with counts reported for FactorVAE and beta-TCVAE does not establish superiority under a common evaluation protocol. Quantitative attribute selectivity, component stability, and matched decoder/preprocessing controls are missing; the explicitly combined 'Gender w/ Mustache' factor also illustrates unresolved entanglement.

The domain-generalization protocol is ambiguous. Appendix A.8 says regularization is selected using a validation split of each dataset, leaving unclear whether target-domain labels influence model selection. The data used to fit PCA and ICA are also unspecified. These details are necessary to establish whether the reported results measure generalization without target supervision.

Reproducibility and reporting are insufficient: synthetic training sample counts and optimization details are missing, real-data results lack uncertainty across repeated runs, and the meaning of synthetic error bars is unspecified. Table 3 also reports the RN101 baseline target average as 20.03, although its four entries average 22.03, overstating the apparent improvement.
